key_insight: An AI system can change even when its public name stays the same. This paper argues for meaningful versioning so researchers and regulators can identify which system they are evaluating.
problem_solved: Providers update models and system integrations without consistently changing public identifiers, making it difficult to reproduce findings and maintain reliable regulatory oversight.
method: Identify the mismatch between changes to AI systems and unchanged public identifiers.
Explain how this mismatch undermines scientific reproducibility and regulatory oversight.
Advocate for AI versioning that serves the needs of researchers and regulators.
impact: Meaningful versioning would help practitioners track system changes and connect evaluations to identifiable AI versions. It would also support more reproducible research and clearer regulatory accountability.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: the same public model name attached to two different system versions.
Layered AI system graphic showing both the model and its surrounding integrations.
Version timeline connecting system updates with corresponding public identifiers.
Research and regulation icons linked to a shared, identifiable AI version.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
